# Approved recipe photograph examples

These reduced-size copies preserve the user's accepted pasta and seven-photo chili examples from this conversation. They are visual regression references and offline provider fixtures, not a production reference library. New jobs always use their own original photographs.

Each source `.jpg` has a corresponding `-approved.jpg` output:

| File prefix | Context that must remain |
| --- | --- |
| 01-ingredients | Separate northern/cannellini beans; original ingredient forms; paper labels; shared spice card listing cumin, salt, oregano, coriander, paprika and chili powder. |
| 02-sauteed-onions | Pale softened onion in a Dutch oven; wooden spoon. |
| 03-onions-and-spices | Onions coated in spices, before liquid is added. |
| 04-broth-and-beans | Clear red broth with beans, tomatoes and corn. |
| 05-chicken-in-broth | Chicken added; broth remains non-creamy; no spoon added. |
| 06-creamy-chili | Opaque creamy chili after cream cheese; cooking pot retained. |
| 07-served-chili | Serving bowls, metal spoon, chips, cheese, board and cloth. |
| 08-skillet | Cooked rigatoni and chicken in a frying pan; thick sauce; retain the frying pan and handles. |

These earlier approved examples establish food, vessel and cooking-stage fidelity. The later v3 profile additionally requires a visibly rearranged ingredient-container layout and visible spoon/utensil color changes in every relevant cooking panel. The default palette is muted blue cookware, dark walnut utensils and a warm beige surface. Wood grain and metallic reflections remain recognizable while color/finish may change. The source angle remains intact. The canonical instructions are in `lib/recipe-intelligence/photoProfile.ts`; the earlier fixtures do not override its newer layout and utensil requirements.

The v4 profile also requires a natural iPhone 17 Pro Max Photo-mode appearance, stronger visible plate/coated-pan color changes, and ingredient labels/layout changes only for ingredient photos. Cooking photos must not acquire extra ingredient bowls or labels. These fixtures remain evidence of source fidelity, not approval of synthetic textures or almost-unchanged vessel colors.

`approved-article.json` is the previously approved Marry Me Chicken Pasta article, retained as a writing reference. It is never used as recipe facts for a different job.

Photo profile v5 uses these fixtures for food and cooking-stage fidelity only. New outputs should have an independent composition while retaining the dish, vessel category/material and meaningful food arrangements. The earlier source angle, exact vessel design and food placement are no longer universal targets. Ingredient groups still move individually with their paper labels. No v5 image has been generated or approved as part of the offline implementation tests; these older outputs do not demonstrate the new visual result or provide rights clearance.
